Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back to the run chase. The players of Nepal can be seen in a huddle near the boundary ropes as they try to pump themselves up before spreading out on the field. The umpires are back out in the middle and it will be the Mosca brothers to open the innings for Italy. Anthony and Justin Mosca are out in the middle and it will be the latter to take strike. Karan KC has the new ball in hand and he is raring to go. Let's play...
... The Run Chase ...

Any chance of a comeback? 124 is a perfect total for Italy to chase down and they will feel they have a chance of making history here. However, Nepal have the spinners to turn it around and their seamers up top can be effective as well. The smaller boundaries and the history of the venue suggest that the chances of Nepal winning this game are bleak, but you never know. Stay tuned as the run chase is up next.

Underwhelming batting display - This is not the Nepal we saw just a few nights ago against the mighty English team. They had their desire to do well and played some smart cricket but in the first 20 overs today, they haven't done justice to their talent. The batting was meek to begin with as they tried to just block in the first 3 overs but they did get to a decent start when the first 6 overs ended. However, barring a couple of batters and Karan KC at the death, there wasn't much to write home about and the likes of Sandeep Lamichhane and Lalit Rajbanshi have a big job on their hands.

Italy's day out with the ball - Spin to win seems to be the mantra at the Wankhede, which is not the usual norm here. Italy have read the conditions perfectly and their spinners have done a fabulous job. The trio of JJ Smuts, Benjamin Manenti and Crishan Kalugamage ruled the roost. Manenti was miserly, Smuts was effective but Kalugamage was prolific in terms of ripping through the Nepal middle-order as he picked up 3 wickets. The pacers did go for a few runs but it didn't matter much as the fielding and catching were spot-on as well.

Advantage Italy at the break - What a stark contrast from the previous game as Italy have stepped up in the field and Nepal seem to have just taken things a bit casual against a side that is ranked lower than them. 123 is a pretty meagre total on the board and right now, the Italians will be feeling really happy with that effort.

Lalit taps it off the front foot in front of cover and hares to the other end. Harry swoops in, picks the ball up and turns around to score a direct hit at the bowling end. Rajbanshi puts in a desperate dive, but to no avail, as he is found short. Nepal have been bowled out for 123!

Commentary.Commentary: With the fall of Dipendra Singh Airee, the umpires have called for a DRINKS BREAK. Italy have done well so far to prevent partnerships from flourishing, and this breakthrough has come at a timely moment for them. Nepal would have used the break to assess when to shift gears, but with Airee's dismissal, the equation changes slightly. Given the resources they possess in the spin department and the assistance spinners have enjoyed on this surface, Nepal will want to get to 150 and back their spinners to defend it, whereas for Italy, it is about continuing to chip away at the wickets. Lokesh Bam joins Aarif Sheikh out in the middle. Bam nearly took Nepal over the line against England.

Commentary.Commentary: Time for the national anthems. It will be Italy's national anthem first, followed by that of Nepal. The anthems are done, and we are all set for the action to commence. As was the case in their game against England, the Nepalese fans are out in numbers once again, and they will surely make their presence felt. Harry Manenti has gathered his troops in a huddle before they head out to the middle. Out walk the two openers of Nepal, Kushal Bhurtel and Aasif Sheikh. Italy are starting with spin. Benjamin Manenti to bowl his off-breaks first up. Bhurtel to face the first ball. Here we go!

PITCH REPORT - Michael Atherton describes the conditions as very toasty, with temperatures touching a high of 34 degrees. Shares that there is a slight cooling breeze offering a bit of relief out in the middle. Informs that the square boundaries measure 65 metres and 64 metres, with 75 metres straight down the ground. Preston Mommsen joins him, and he mentions that this is the same wicket on which England played West Indies last night and in that game, spinners had a major say. Considering the heat and the dry nature of the surface, Preston reckons that spinners will play a key role. Atherton further says that last night, Adil Rashid managed to get the ball to turn significantly, both with his leg-breaks and his googlies. He adds that the Wankhede Stadium has produced more turn in this World Cup than any other venue so far.

Italy (Playing XI) - Anthony Mosca, Justin Mosca, JJ Smuts, Harry Manenti (C), Benjamin Manenti, Marcus Campopiano (In for Wayne Madsen), Grant Stewart, Gian-Piero Meade (WK), Jaspreet Singh (In for Thomas Draca), Crishan Kalugamage, and Ali Hasan.

Nepal (Playing XI) - Kushal Bhurtel, Aasif Sheikh (WK), Rohit Paudel (C), Dipendra Singh Airee, Aarif Sheikh, Lokesh Bam, Gulshan Jha, Karan KC, Nandan Yadav, Sandeep Lamichhane, and Lalit Rajbanshi (In for Sher Malla).

The skipper of Nepal - Rohit Paudel says that they would have bowled first as well. Adds that they will look to make the most of the wicket, which is the same one that they played on last time, and believes it will turn in the second innings. Mentions that it is a privilege to play all games at the same venue, and they know the Asian conditions well. Feels that they need to be more clinical in all departments of the game and applauds the fans who support them so well.

The captain of Italy - Harry Manenti feels there is a bit of moisture in the wicket, and they want to make the most of it. Mentions they want to utilise the new ball up front. He admits there were some nerves in the opening game and that a few things went against them. Believes that losing their skipper, Wayne Madsen, was the turning point. Harry acknowledges that they are up against teams ranked well above them, but says the side strongly believes in its own abilities. He adds that it is pretty exciting to be here and competing against some impressive sides, with Nepal being one of them. Shares that it is a privilege to lead Italy. Informs that Marcus Campopiano comes into the side, who has played a lot of cricket for Italy. Also informs that Thomas Draca misses out, and Jaspreet Singh comes in for him.

TOSS - Toss time in Mumbai! Harry Manenti is out in the middle as Italy's captain, which confirms that Wayne Madsen is out of this clash. Rohit Paudel is the captain for Nepal. Italy win the toss and will BOWL first.

A thumping win for Sri Lanka - In the first game of the day in Kandy, Dasun Shanaka’s men have handed Oman a comprehensive drubbing. Riding on three fifties from their top five, Sri Lanka posted 225. In reply, Oman never really got going and could only muster 120. The 105-run win lifts Shanaka’s side to the top of Group B after they began the game in third.

Who'll take the spoils? Nepal’s ability to deploy high-quality spin against an Italian lineup that traditionally favors pace could be the deciding factor, especially with Sher Malla and Lamichhane looking to exploit any turn under the afternoon sun. Italy’s best chance lies in their power-hitting. If they can use the short Wankhede boundaries to their advantage and post a total exceeding 180, they could pressure a Nepali side that has occasionally struggled with clinical finishes. Stay tuned as the toss and team sheets are coming up shortly.

Debutants looking to step up - Italy, meanwhile, are navigating a historic but challenging maiden World Cup campaign. After a tough opening loss to Scotland in Kolkata, the Azzurri are looking to find their footing on the batting-friendly red soil of Mumbai. The Italians have leaned heavily on their Global Italian core, featuring seasoned professionals like JJ Smuts and the Manenti brothers (Benjamin and Harry), who bring significant T20 franchise experience to the squad. However, the health of captain Wayne Madsen remains a major talking point and his shoulder injury during the first match has left a leadership void that the squad must fill if they hope to counter Nepal’s aggressive brand of cricket.

Nepal's second home - Nepal enter this clash as the more experienced side in major ICC events, having recently pushed England to the absolute limit in a nail-biting five-run thriller at this very venue. Rohit Paudel’s men have effectively turned Mumbai into a second home, backed by a massive and vocal expatriate fanbase that provides a home-field atmosphere. With their top order finding rhythm and a spin attack led by the world-class Sandeep Lamichhane, the 'Rhinos' are eager to translate their near-misses into a vital win that keeps their Super 8 aspirations alive.

Welcome to the coverage - Hello, and a warm welcome to our coverage of the ICC Men's T20 World Cup, 2026. Match 17 features a clash between Nepal and Italy. Two teams who are eager to prove that they belong on the biggest stage, but only one can reign supreme. Both teams have started their campaigns with a loss, but the manner of the losses was very contrasting.
... MATCH DAY ...

Heartbreak, hope and a group on the Line - Two T20 World Cups, two cruel heartbreaks for Nepal, edged by a single run against South Africa in 2024 and then falling four short against England in this edition, yet their refusal to go quietly and the fight they bring every time sets the tone as they head into a crucial Group C clash against Italy at the Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai. This is a game that could have a major say in how this group shapes up, with both teams coming in desperate to get their campaign back on track after opening-round defeats and knowing that another loss would leave their qualification hopes hanging by a thread. Resilient Nepal ready to strike back - Since the last World Cup, Nepal have quietly built a strong body of work in this format, highlighted by a 2-1 T20I series win over West Indies in 2025. That confidence runs through a batting group anchored by Kushal Bhurtel and Aasif Sheikh at the top, the two highest scorers in T20Is for them in 2025. Skipper Rohit Paudel provides stability in the middle, while Deependra Singh Airee continues to be their most influential all-rounder, as he showed again against England with a fine all-round display. Lokesh Bam will be itching to put things right after being left stranded at the end of a superb knock in that narrow defeat. With the ball, Sandeep Lamichhane remains their biggest weapon with his leggies and googlies, and he is their leading wicket-taker in this format. He is supported by the pace of Karan KC and Nandan Yadav. Nepal also have growing variety in their attack, with Sher Malla making an immediate impact on debut by removing Salt with his very first delivery. Even so, Nepal will be keen to tighten their execution at the death after letting England slip away late. Debutants under pressure - Italy, meanwhile, are still trying to settle into life at their first-ever T20 World Cup, coming off a disappointing loss to Scotland that was made even harder by the injury to captain Wayne Madsen, whose dislocated left shoulder threatens to rule him out of the rest of the tournament, a particularly cruel twist after finally achieving his World Cup dream at the age of 42. Although the pressure of the big stage may have shown in that opening game, there were encouraging signs with the Manenti brothers among the runs and Benjamin registering a half-century, while the Mosca brothers, Justin and Anthony, will be key at the top in providing brisk starts to set the tone. In Madsen's absence, the responsibility will fall heavily on the power of JJ Smuts and the all-round skills of Grant Stewart, backed by a bowling group led by Ali Hasan and Thomas Draca with Crishan Kalugamage offering spin support, making this a contest where Nepal's experience of tight World Cup battles meets an Italian side eager to prove that their historic qualification was only the beginning. Team Form (Last 5 T20Is, latest result first) - Nepal - LWWWW | Italy - LWLLL. What to expect? What adds another layer to this contest is the venue factor, with Nepal already having played a high-scoring thriller here against England and knowing exactly how the Wankhede plays, while Italy arrive from Eden Gardens in Kolkata and will need to adjust quickly to different conditions, making this a game where early momentum, smart bowling at the death and the ability to adapt could prove decisive in a clash that promises plenty of runs and high drama. Whose side are you on?
